```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=4)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Analytical question

State the analyte, matrix, sample scope, quantity and unit. Name the unit of the
course you are working on. All supplied datasets are simulated teaching data.

## Data and preparation

The initial example below checks the introductory water dataset so the template
renders immediately. Replace it with the imports and records for your chosen
lesson. Keep this source at the project root.

```{r import}
data <- read_csv("data/course/water.csv", show_col_types=FALSE)
knitr::kable(head(data))
```

Explain one row, independent samples versus repeat readings, and the mass or
volume chain connecting original material to the measured solution. Preserve
sample and preparation identifiers.

## Chemical relationship and calculation

Add the chemical equation or measurement model, its unit convention and its
assumptions. Include the necessary calibration and diagnostic plots for the
chosen method. Keep unrounded values in code.

## Checks and reporting decisions

Give the relevant blank, range, independent QC, matrix/recovery and separation
evidence. Include a table with supported values and explicit withheld reasons.
A withheld estimate is not zero analyte.

## Uncertainty and limitations

State what each uncertainty or interval describes, which sources are included,
and which sources are omitted. Do not imply a full method uncertainty from a
reading SD alone.

## Transfer task and conclusion

Complete the chosen lesson's transfer task. Explain the chemical conclusion and
next analytical action. Save CSV results in output/. Restart R and render again.
